ENGLISH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #13
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

2. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

3. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

4. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

5. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

6. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

10. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

11. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. run

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

14. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

15. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. goes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Intonation in sentences: Question tags and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Intonation in sentences: Question tags and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
